text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyHow Wishful Thinking Impacts Political PolarizationAnd vice versaJCBy Jake Currie12:33 PM CST on November 3, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHappy(?) election day! Powered By 10 ShareNextStayAs you may have noticed, our country has been gripped by intense political polarization for quite some time. According to a recent study in Political Behavior, on the other side of the polarization coin is wishful thinking—the belief that your party will emerge victorious—and the two phenomena are related.“As I read about wishful thinking, I realized there’s a flip side when it comes to politics,” study author Seth Warner of the University of Connecticut explained in a statement. “If you’re a Democrat, you want Democrats to win. If you’re a Republican, you want Republicans to win. But today, it’s just as likely that if you’re a Democrat, you don’t want Republicans to win. If you’re a Republican, you don’t want Democrats to win. There’s a negative valence to wishful thinking that to this point hasn’t been explored.”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
